requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of IPv4 ICMP redirects on node1.
requirements.summary: A root-owned sysctl policy sets accept_redirects=0 for all, default, and wildcard interfaces. Direct checks showed 0 for all existing interfaces before and after a reboot, demonstrating both active and persistent enforcement.

requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of IPv4 source-routed packets on node1.
requirements.summary: The persistent policy sets accept_source_route=0 for all, default, and wildcard interfaces. Direct checks showed 0 for all existing interfaces before and after a reboot.

overall_summary: Both required IPv4 hardening outcomes are satisfied. The node-restart protocol is coherent: node1 was healthy before restart, the restart was acknowledged, its boot ID changed from 96974ac3-f19e-45f7-9672-e880dd505cf8 to 4d5cda1c-b9af-40dd-90ce-7391c715db41, and it recovered to a running state with the policy file and hardened runtime values intact. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the reboot, while post-run service, socket, and package observations show healthy recovery.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating, permissioning, and applying the sysctl policy was directly required (cmd-88970254e05c4466). Scheduling the reboot was required by the provider restart protocol and also validated persistence (cmd-b0ed6592b3244441). The transient connection timeout and starting state were expected during the bounded reboot; recovery completed without failed services, package damage, new exposure, or abandoned temporary files.
